groups.title: Soft Capsule (E19400ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Those over 7 years of age and under 15 years of age: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby (newborn) under 3 months of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergy caused by a medicine (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Do not drink alcohol while taking it. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. Do not take it continuously for a long period.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you are being given another medicine such as barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid or flucloxacillin.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever and the like) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.caution:

groups.title: Tablet (101305ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, pain from a sprain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Children aged 12 years and older and adults: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day (every 4 to 6 hours) when needed.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment or severely reduced heart function; if you have had aspirin asthma (an asthma attack triggered by a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine); or if you have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had liver impairment, kidney impairment, peptic ulcer or a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have impaired heart function; if you have had hypersensitivity; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are an older person; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Without the instruction of a doctor or pharmacist, adults must not take it for pain for 10 days or more and children must not take it for 5 days or more, and it must not be taken for fever for 3 days or more. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. If pain or fever persists or worsens, or if a new symptom appears, consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with another anti-inflammatory analgesic. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you take lithium or a thiazide diuretic. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you take warfarin long term.

If signs of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria and the like), an asthma attack, thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, difficulty breathing, sweating, low blood pressure, shock), nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal problems on long-term use such as gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer or perforation, rash, allergic reactions, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), raised AST, raised ALT or fixed drug eruption occurs, or if pain or fever persists or worsens or a new symptom appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for primary and secondary carnitine deficiency and for disturbance of heart muscle metabolism caused by ischaemic heart disease such as angina and acute myocardial infarction.
groups.usage: Adults: take 2 to 3 g in 1 day, divided into 2 to 3 doses in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Transient nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, body odour, rash, urticaria, swelling of the face or mild muscle weakness may occur.

groups.title: Capsule (153101ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to loosen mucus and help bring up sputum in acute and chronic respiratory disease.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 3 times in 1 day. When it is taken for an acute respiratory condition, do not take it continuously for 10 days or more.
groups.caution:
This medicine is not for people with hypersensitivity to it, liver cirrhosis, cystathionine synthase deficiency, peptic ulcer or severe kidney impairment (creatinine clearance below 25 mL/min).

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have mild or moderate liver impairment, or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a cough medicine.

Headache, cold symptoms, difficulty breathing, taste disturbance, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, upper abdominal pain, abdominal pain, heartburn, urticaria, erythema or eczema may occur.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E69000ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acute night-time pain with temporary sleeplessness caused by the pain.
groups.usage: Adults who have difficulty sleeping because of pain: take 1 to 2 capsules per dose, 1 time in 1 day, before bedtime. Including this medicine, do not exceed 1200 mg of ibuprofen and 75 mg of diphenhydramine within 24 hours. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours after taking ibuprofen and/or diphenhydramine. If the cause of the symptoms has not been identified, do not take it continuously for more than 5 days.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Taking this medicine may cause serious and possibly fatal gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as bleeding, ulceration and perforation of the gastrointestinal tract.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have difficulty breathing due to an asthma attack, emphysema or chronic bronchitis; if you have or have had hypersensitivity such as asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if you have a severe blood disorder, liver impairment, kidney impairment, cardiac insufficiency or high blood pressure; if pain occurs before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); if you have glaucoma or an obstructive disease of the lower urinary tract such as prostatic hyperplasia; if you have a convulsive disorder such as epilepsy; if you have phaeochromocytoma; if you have insomnia without pain or pain without insomnia; if the user is a child under 15 years of age; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a blood disorder or a tendency to bleed; if you have liver cirrhosis, liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have cardiac insufficiency or heart disease or high blood pressure; if you have hypersensitivity; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD); if you have ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease; if you have myasthenia gravis, diabetes or thyroid disease; if you are an older person aged 65 years and older or the user is a child; or if you take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke.

Do not take more than the recommended dose. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Take care when driving or operating machinery. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 5 days of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an ACE inhibitor, lithium, furosemide or a thiazide diuretic, methotrexate, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, another sleep aid, a hypnotic sedative, an MAO inhibitor, a cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic (for example aspirin, acetaminophen or naproxen), an antitussive-expectorant, an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine), another medicine containing ibuprofen or diphenhydramine, or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: shock or an anaphylactoid reaction, heartburn, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure; blood disorders such as reduced haematocrit or haemoglobin, anaemia, aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, reduced granulocytes, white blood cells or platelets, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), a photosensitivity reaction, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, angioneurotic oedema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; hepatitis, jaundice, raised GOT, GPT or alkaline phosphatase (ALP), liver impairment; an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing; groups.title: Soft Capsule (E58200ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins A, B1 and B2 in physical tiredness, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, and in old age. Through the vitamins it contains, this medicine is used for the relief of night blindness, beriberi, eye strain and dryness of the eyes, and of neuralgia, muscle pain, back pain, joint pain such as stiff shoulders, angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 8 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If a pregnant woman takes 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A in 1 day, it may cause birth defects. Women within the first 3 months of pregnancy and women who may be pregnant must not take it.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to soybean oil; if you have hypersensitivity to soybean or peanut; or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Red No. 40; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis; if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; or if you have fat overload.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. The vitamin A in this medicine is supplied sufficiently by a normal diet, so the supplementary dose must not exceed 5,000 IU in 1 day. Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. It may turn the urine yellow and so affect clinical test values. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful swelling of the joints, loose stools, diarrhoea, constipation, loss of appetite, red spots, urticaria, eczema, rash, maculopapular rash, itching, or oedema or fluid retention in people with kidney failure or heart failure occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults: for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, take 1 to 3 capsules (200 to 600 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day, up to 16 capsules (3200 mg) in 1 day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight in 1 day, divided into 3 to 4 doses. For mild to moderate pain or a cold, adults: take 1 to 2 capsules (200 to 400 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. For migraine, adults: take 1 to 2 capsules (200 to 400 mg) per dose, without exceeding 2 capsules within 24 hours. Adolescents aged 12 years and older: take 1 to 2 capsules (200 to 400 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. If the body weight is less than 30 kg, the amount in 1 day must not exceed 500 mg, and it is better to avoid taking it on an empty stomach.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have or have had hypersensitivity such as asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if pain occurs before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; or if you are in the last 3 months of pregnancy.

groups.title: Enteric-coated Tablet (C96000ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of constipation, loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids.
groups.usage: Those aged 15 years and older: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses. At first take the smallest amount, then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool. Do not chew the tablet when taking it.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like) or intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you are on a sodium-restricted diet; if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 203 or Quinoline Yellow WS.

If symptoms do not improve after taking it for 1 week, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Unless it is really necessary, children aged 10 years or younger should avoid taking it.

Do not take this medicine within 1 hour after an antacid or after drinking milk.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to improve liver function in chronic liver disease and to improve physical tiredness and general lassitude caused by impaired liver function.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child; if you have severe obstruction of the bile duct or fulminant hepatitis; if you have large or small bowel inflammation such as Crohn's disease; if you have radio-opaque calcified gallstones, a non-functioning gallbladder or acute cholecystitis; if you have kidney disease; or if you have peptic ulcer (acute gastric or duodenal ulcer).

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe pancreatic disease or gallstones.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with an oral diabetes medicine (tolbutamide), cholestyramine, colestipol, medicinal charcoal, antacids containing magnesium or aluminium hydroxide, medicines that reduce cholesterol in the bile (for example oral contraceptives containing oestrogen), medicines that reduce cholesterol in the blood (for example clofibrate), or medicines that damage the liver.

If diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, constipation, heartburn, stomach discomfort, itching, rash, general lassitude, dizziness, calcification of gallstones, raised liver enzyme values (ALT, ALP, AST, gamma-GT), reduced white blood cells, or interstitial pneumonia with fever, cough, difficulty breathing and abnormal chest X-ray occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Enteric-coated Tablet (D53100ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that follow constipation.
groups.usage: Adults aged 15 years and older: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 1 time in 1 day, at bedtime. For the first dose take the smallest amount, then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal disease such as appendicitis, intestinal bleeding or ulcerative colitis; if you have intestinal obstruction; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child aged 10 years or younger; if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have an allergic constitution; if you are on a sodium-restricted diet; or if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Do not keep taking it for 1 week or more. Do not chew this medicine when taking it. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take this medicine within 1 hour after taking an antacid or drinking milk. (Avoid drinking milk or taking an antacid within 1 hour after taking this medicine.)

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Constipation and the loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal intestinal fermentation and haemorrhoids that follow it

groups.title: Syrup (142334ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to reduce fever caused by an acute upper respiratory tract infection.
groups.usage: Children aged 6 months and older: take 0.4 to 0.6 mL per kg of body weight (5 to 7 mg per kg) per dose at intervals of 4 to 6 hours when needed, without exceeding 4 doses (28 mg per kg) in 1 day. For a child weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed 25 mL (300 mg) in 1 day. If the body weight is known, dosing by body weight is more appropriate; refer to the approved product information for the recommended dose for each age group.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, liver impairment, kidney impairment, heart failure or high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergy caused by aspirin or another anti-inflammatory analgesic; if it is for the treatment of pain before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had peptic ulcer, a blood disorder, a tendency to bleed, liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have heart failure or high blood pressure; if you have a history of hypersensitivity; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease; if you have ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease; if you are an older person or the user is a child; if you have stomach cancer; if you take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke; or if the user is a baby under 6 months of age.

When it is taken for a long period, as a rule this should be within 5 days.

Do not use it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Consult a pharmacist if you use it together with a glucocorticoid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, a diuretic with an antihypertensive, an ACE inhibitor, furosemide, lithium, low-dose methotrexate or a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like).

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely signs of shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure); aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function or eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or Lyell's syndrome (toxic epidermal necrolysis); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; jaundice, raised GOT, GPT or AL-P; triggering of an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura; loss of vision or scotoma; aseptic meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness); reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium; occasionally rash or itching.

Reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude, acute pulmonary oedema, occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort or swelling around the eye sockets, rarely hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, a fall or rise in blood pressure or palpitations, and very rarely thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, constipation, malaise, fever or nosebleed may occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Reducing fever caused by an acute upper respiratory tract infection

groups.title: Soft Capsule (D65500ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child under 2 years of age; if you have a constitution prone to allergy or have had allergic symptoms (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not take it continuously for a long period. Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after about 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Do not take this medicine if you have stopped taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) within the past 2 weeks. Consult a pharmacist if you have been given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, or another medicine such as a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, signs of shock (rarely urticaria, swelling and chest tightness after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, a severe skin adverse reaction such as fever, erythema and many small pustules, asthma, general lassitude, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) or symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance and the like) occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Relief of cold symptoms (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint and muscle pain)

groups.title: Tablet (E73100ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins D, B1, B2 and B6 in physical tiredness, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, during growth and in old age, for poor development of the bones and teeth, for the prevention of rickets, for the relief of beriberi, eye strain, neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulders and the like), angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis, and for the supply of zinc.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day, after a meal.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have hypersensitivity to soybean or peanut; if you have had an allergic reaction to soybean oil; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have high blood calcium (an excess of calcium in the blood); if you have sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause) or kidney disease; or if you have severe renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have or have had kidney stones; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; if you are at particular risk from fat overload; if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if the user is a child who gets plenty of sunlight and eats a normal diet; or if you are short of folic acid.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. It may turn the urine yellow and so affect clinical test values. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with a phosphate, a calcium salt, an oral tetracycline preparation, an antacid or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an antialdosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loose stools, red spots, cardiac arrest, reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or pulmonary oedema occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins D, B1, B2 and B6 and of zinc, poor bone and tooth development, prevention of rickets, beriberi, eye strain, neuralgia, muscle and joint pain, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis

groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule per dose, 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with a phosphate, a calcium salt, an oral tetracycline preparation or an antacid. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash (reddening of the skin), red spots, cardiac arrest or reduced central nervous system function occurs, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected, becomes heavier or bleeding lasts longer, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of blocked nose, runny nose, sneezing, watering eyes, sore throat and a heavy head caused by a nasal cold (acute rhinitis), allergic rhinitis or sinusitis.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours.
groups.caution:
If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if the user is a child under 15 years of age; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure; or if you have severe acute or chronic kidney disease or renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have high blood pressure, heart disease, kidney disease, oedema, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you are an older person; if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appear in connection with pseudoephedrine; or if a cold medicine, an antitussive-expectorant or an oral medicine for rhinitis has ever caused insomnia, vertigo, weakness, tremor or palpitations.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with another oral medicine for rhinitis or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (cold medicine, antitussive-expectorant, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine and the like). Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If haemorrhagic stroke, nausea and vomiting, persistent or severe thirst, constipation, loss of appetite, rash and reddening of the skin, itching, difficulty passing urine, headache, facial flushing, abnormal sensitivity to light, or, rarely, shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing and the like), pseudoaldosteronism (reduced urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, raised blood pressure, headache and the like), myopathy (weakness, cramps of the limbs, paralysis and the like), or posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance and the like) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.
